title: Monday demonstrations in East Germany
text: The Monday demonstrations were a series of peaceful political protests against the government of the German Democratic Republic (GDR). The demonstrations began in Leipzig on 4 September 1989, starting the Peaceful Revolution in the GDR: the fall of the Berlin Wall, the collapse of the government, and German reunification.

title: Die Wende and Peaceful Revolution
text: The Peaceful Revolution – also called Die Wende (German pronunciation: , "the turn" or "the turning point") – was one of the peaceful revolutions of 1989 at the peak of the collapse of the Eastern Bloc in the late 1980s. It was a process of sociopolitical change that led to, among other openings, the opening of East Germany's borders to the Western world.

title: 10–21 February - 39th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 39th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 10 to 21 February 1989. The Golden Bear was awarded to American film Rain Man directed by Barry Levinson.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1989
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 1989 with the song "Flieger", composed by Dieter Bohlen, with lyrics by Joachim Horn-Bernges, and performed by Nino de Angelo. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Bayerischer Rundfunk, selected their entry through a national final.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1989

title: 20–30 July - The World Games take place in Karlsruhe.
text: The 1989 World Games, commonly known as Karlsruhe 1989, were the third edition of the World Games, an international multi-sport event. This edition was held in Karlsruhe, West Germany.

title: Pan-European Picnic
text: The Pan-European Picnic was a peace demonstration held on the Austro-Hungarian border near Sopron, Hungary, on 19 August 1989. The opening of the border gate between Austria and Hungary at the Pan-European Picnic was an event in the chain reaction, at the end of which Germany reunified, the Iron Curtain fell apart, and the Eastern Bloc disintegrated.

title: East German Republic Day Parade of 1989
text: The East German Republic Day Parade of 1989 was a parade of the National People's Army on Karl-Marx-Allee (between Strausberger Platz and Alexanderplatz) in East Berlin on 7 October 1989 commemorating the 40th anniversary of the establishment of East Germany.
wiki: East German Republic Day Parade of 1989

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
text: The Fall of the Berlin Wall and the fortified inner German border occurred immediately... without delay after a Politburo press conference on 9 November 1989 prematurely announced that East Germans could travel without restrictions after, in the decades before, hundreds had been killed by Border Troops of the German Democratic Republic when trying to sneak through the Iron Curtain.

title: First citizens' occupation of a Stasi building
text: The Memorial and Education Centre Andreasstraße, is a museum in Erfurt, Germany, which is housed in a former prison used by the East German Ministry for State Security (Stasi). It is informally known as the Stasi Museum.

title: “Don't Worry, Be Happy” by Bobby McFerrin
text: "Don't Worry, Be Happy" is a 1988 song by Bobby McFerrin, released as the lead single from his album Simple Pleasures. It was the first a cappella song to reach number-one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, a position it held for two weeks.

title: “First Time” by 16 January
text: "First Time" is a song by American singer Robin Beck from her second album, Trouble or Nothin'. The song was released as a single in July 1988 and was originally recorded for a Coca-Cola commercial.

title: “Something's Gotten Hold of My Heart” by 6 March

title: “Looking for Freedom” by 3 April
text: "Looking for Freedom" is a song written by German music producer Jack White, originally released in 1978 by German singer Marc Seaberg and featured on his 1979 album California Gold. It was covered in German later that year under the title "Auf der Straße nach Süden" by Tony Marshall.

title: “The Look” by 29 May
text: "The Look" is a song by Swedish pop duo Roxette. It was released in early 1989 as the fourth single from their second studio album, Look Sharp!

title: “Das Omen (Teil I)” by Mysterious Art
text: Mysterious Art is a German electronic dance music group founded in 1987. The group became famous for its hit single "Das Omen”.

title: “Swing the Mood” by 4 September
text: "Swing the Mood" is a song by British novelty pop music act Jive Bunny and the Mastermixers, released as the first single from their debut album, Jive Bunny: The Album. Produced by the father and son DJ team of Andy and John Pickles, "Swing the Mood" is a cut and paste record which fused a number of early rock and roll records with liberal use of Glenn Miller's "In the Mood".

title: “Lambada” by 25 September
text: "Lambada", also known as "Chorando Se Foi" or "Llorando se fue (Lambada)" (both meaning "crying, he/she went away" in Portuguese and Spanish, respectively), is a song by French-Brazilian pop group Kaoma. With vocals by Brazilian vocalist Loalwa Braz, the song was released as Kaoma's debut single and included on their debut album, Worldbeat.

title: “Another Day in Paradise” by Phil Collins
text: "Another Day in Paradise" is a song written and recorded by the English musician Phil Collins. Produced by Collins along with Hugh Padgham, it was released as the first single from his number-one album ...But Seriously.
